sections.title: The letter dzsé
paragraphs: The letter (dzsé) /dʒeː/ makes the sound you hear in (dzsem) /ˈd͡ʒɛm/, which means jam. This letter has only one sound in Hungarian. It is a single unit in the Hungarian alphabet.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: This sound is an affricate. An affricate is a consonant that starts as a plosive and ends as a fricative. Put the tip of your tongue behind the upper front teeth to block the air. Release the air slowly through a small gap. Turn your voice on so your vocal cords buzz. Feel your throat shake with your fingers.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: This letter always makes the same sound in all positions. You hear it at the start of (dzsem) /ˈd͡ʒɛm/. You also hear it in the middle of words like (tiniédzser) /ˈtini.eːd͡ʒɛr/.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: This sound is very close to the j in the English word jam. Do not turn off your voice. If your voice stops, it sounds like the ch in cheer. Keep your vocal cords vibrating from the start to the finish.
